1. It is an explicit instance binder of the theorem, so it is an argument.
2. The statement still elaborates without it. `Representation.character` is defined as `LinearMap.trace k V (ρ g)`. In Mathlib it sits in a section that has `[FiniteDimensional k V]` as a variable. But a definition only takes the section variables its body uses. To confirm the definition does not take the instance, look at `char_mul_comm` and `char_iso`: both mention `ρ.character` and are stated under `omit [FiniteDimensional k V] in`, and they compile. Nothing else in the statement mentions finite-dimensionality. The sum over `GL2 q` only needs a `Fintype` instance on the group.
3. It is a plain deletion.
4. The statement is still true without it. Take any nonzero v, which exists by `Nontrivial V`. Since `GL2 q` is finite, the span of the orbit {ρ g v} is a finitely generated submodule. It is stable under ρ, so it gives a `Subrepresentation` (a submodule plus the `apply_mem_toSubmodule` field). It is nonzero, so `hirr` makes it equal to ⊤. Hence V is finitely generated, i.e. finite-dimensional.
5. The proof works. A proof can first derive `FiniteDimensional K V` as above and then run the original proof unchanged. In current Mathlib this step is not even needed: `Representation.char_orthonormal` is stated under `[Fintype G] [Invertible (Nat.card G : k)] [IsAlgClosed k] [IsIrreducible ρ] [IsIrreducible σ]` and derives finite-dimensionality internally via `ρ.asModuleEquiv.finiteDimensional`. The rest of the existing proof uses only `hirr`, `Nontrivial V`, `CharZero K` and `IsAlgClosed K`.
